I will keep the land in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, and for me this is the safest way to make grain from one piece of land in one year. The climate here fits it: wheat uses the cool season, maize uses the hot rainy season, and I do not need to gamble on vegetables, cotton, or peanuts. At my age, I also want a system I know well, with work concentrated into a few key periods and with machinery services easy to hire if needed.

Since it is the start of the growing season, my winter wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so I will manage that crop through harvest first. I will keep fertilizer moderate instead of pushing for the highest possible yield, because I care about stable output, lower cash cost, and less risk from lodging, drought, and waste. Wheat needs the irrigation more here, so I will give the water to wheat at the important stages and keep maize lighter on irrigation because summer rain usually carries more of that crop. After wheat harvest, I will return the straw, do light land preparation, and put in summer maize quickly so I do not lose moisture or time. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stand uniformity and dependable yield, not because I want to manage a complicated system. I will keep pesticide use limited to the times when I think it is necessary to hold the crop steady.
